propositions: The review-bot receiver logs the webhook token in plaintext within the uvicorn access log query string on every /webhook and /rerun request, exposing GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN to journald and any log-grepping operation.
The webhook and rerun endpoints accept the shared secret as a query parameter (?token=...), which uvicorn's default access logging captures and writes to stderr/journald in clear text.
The exposed credential serves as authentication for both endpoints and as a Gerrit bot credential, allowing any journal reader to drive reviews and act against Gerrit.
The fix moves the token from the query string to the X-Rebar-Token HTTP header (which access logs do not record) for both endpoints, with TokenRedactingFilter installed as a backstop redaction layer.
The runbook infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md /rerun recipe must no longer instruct operators to put the token in a URL, and a rotation note must be added.
The previously-logged token must be rotated and the rotation explicitly recorded, since the code fix does not erase existing journal entries containing the compromised credential.
